english.title: Operator/master of ship in which dangerous goods or marine pollutants were not carried in accordance with code

additionalkeywords.additionalkeyword: Merchant Shipping Dangerous Goods and Marine Pollutants Regulations 1997

english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) were the

(A)_[operator]_
(B)_[master]_

of **(..SPECIFY SHIP..) in which

(C)_[dangerous goods,]_
(D)_[marine pollutants,]_

namely **(..SPECIFY GOODS OR POLLUTANTS..), were carried

(E)_[being goods listed in Chapter VI of the BCH Code and which were not handled or carried in accordance with the requirements of that code]_
(F)_[being goods listed in Chapter 17 of the IBC Code and which were not handled or carried in accordance with the requirements of that code]_
(G)_[being goods listed in Chapter XIX of the Gas Carrier Code and which were not handled or carried in accordance with the requirements of that code]_
(H)_[being goods listed in Chapter XIX of the Gas Carrier Code for Existing Ships and which were not handled or carried in accordance with the requirements of that code]_
(I)_[being goods listed in Chapter 19 of the IGC Code and which were not handled or carried in accordance with the requirements of that code]_
(J)_[being classified dangerous goods listed in Appendix 1 of the IMSBC Code and which were not handled or carried in accordance with the requirements of that code]_
(K)_[being goods, which consisted of a liquid chemical which was not listed in the Codes mentioned in regulation 20(2)(a) of the Merchant Shipping (Dangerous Goods and Marine Pollutants) Regulations 1997 and, which were not handled or carried in accordance with an approval given in writing by the Secretary of State]_
(L)_[being goods, which consisted of a liquefied gas which was not listed in the Codes mentioned in regulation 20(2)(a) of the Merchant Shipping (Dangerous Goods and Marine Pollutants) Regulations 1997 and, which were not handled or carried in accordance with an approval given in writing by the Secretary of State]_

english.legislation: Contrary to regulations 20(2) and (3) and 24 of the Merchant Shipping (Dangerous Goods and Marine Pollutants) Regulations 1997.

english.notes:
(i) Regulation 23 of the Merchant Shipping (Dangerous Goods and Marine Pollutants) Regulations 1997 provides that in any case where a ship does not comply with the requirements of these Regulations the ship shall be liable to be detained and section 284 of the Merchant Shipping Act 1995 (which relates to the detention of a ship) shall have effect in relation to the ship, subject to the modification that as if for the words "this Act", wherever they appear, there were substituted the words "the Merchant Shipping (Dangerous Goods and Marine Pollutants) Regulations 1997".
(ii) Regulation 23 of the Merchant Shipping (Dangerous Goods and Marine Pollutants) Regulations 1997 provides that where the commission by any person of this offence is due to the act or default of some other person, that other person shall be guilty of the offence, and a person may be charged with and convicted of the offence by virtue of this regulation whether or not proceedings are taken against the first-mentioned person.
(iii) Regulation 24(2) provides in any proceedings for this offence it shall be a defence for a person to prove that:-
(a) all reasonable steps had been taken by him to ensure compliance with the Regulations; or
(b) he did not know nor ought to have known nor had reasonable grounds for suspecting the goods to be dangerous goods or marine pollutants as the case may be; or
(c) that the goods were handled and carried in accordance with the provisions of the IMDG Code where appropriate; or
(d) if the person charged is the operator or master, in the case of goods packed in a freight container or vehicle, that before the freight container or vehicle was taken on board the ship the person responsible for packing the goods into the freight container or vehicle had provided the operator or master of the ship with a signed packing certificate certifying that the goods had been properly packed in the freight container or vehicle; or
(e) the goods being solid dangerous goods in bulk were being handled and carried in accordance with the I.M.S.B.C. Code; or
(f) the goods being liquid chemical or gaseous dangerous goods in bulk such goods were being handled and carried in accordance with the relevant requirements of the BCH Code, the IBC Code, the Gas Carrier Code, the Gas Carrier Code for Existing Ships or the IGC Code;
(g) the goods were being carried in accordance with Merchant Shipping Notices MSN 1705 or MSN 1706 where appropriate

other.penalty:
Summary: A fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: Two years imprisonment and / or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None
